races.name: Michael Brunton Memorial British EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Arctic Tsar
runners_data.note: Raced twice at 6f on Good, finishing 6th and 8th, but Clive Cox's operation often improves sharply between runs and Joe Leavy gets a prominent-tracking ride that suits the likely pace shape here.

runners_data.name: Easy Answer
runners_data.note: Michael Bell's hold-up performer showed a 3rd at 6f on Good last time but is a true rear-end type whose best chance depends on a stronger-than-expected gallop; racing closer than ideal reduces the late-surge option.

runners_data.name: First Mate
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's hold-up runner has two 7th-place finishes at 6f on Good and, while Tom Marquand is an intelligent judge of pace, this horse will not be in its natural rearward berth given the field dynamics and that tempers its claims.

runners_data.name: Flick Of An Eye
runners_data.note: David Probert's unraced juvenile for Simon & Ed Crisford carries Unknown going/style tags but the yard is in strong T14 form (6/22) and any debut juvenile with natural early stride will slot into a prominent spot behind the leader on fast ground.

runners_data.name: Gold Reef City
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's hold-up type has a 3rd at 6f on Good in the book and the same trainer also runs Saturn Star, so Robbie Downey's tactical instructions will be worth watching as a race-day clue.

runners_data.name: Goodwood Meteor
runners_data.note: Marcus Tregoning's runner has run 6th and 9th at 6f on Good and Soft and is on a short yard turnaround (2/7 in 14 days); going form at Good to Firm is untested, which is a mild concern on today's surface.

runners_data.name: Hackpen Hill
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's confirmed front-runner wears a hood and has run twice at 6f on Good without winning, but the key asset here is a clear lead from flag to finish with Kieran Shoemark in the saddle and no rival capable of pressing him early.

runners_data.name: Ongombo
runners_data.note: Charlie Fellowes' hold-up type has run twice at 6f on Standard (AW), making today's Good to Firm turf debut a genuine unknown; Paddy Bradley's booking is low-profile and the 44-day break adds further uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Saturn Star
runners_data.note: Second Beckett runner alongside Gold Reef City, making its debut with Unknown style and going tags; Hector Crouch rides and yard form at T14 (4/39) is modest, so this represents a speculative entry rather than a yard banker.

runners_data.name: Forbidden Fire
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's unraced debutant gets the plum booking of Oisin Murphy, and Balding's T14 strike rate of 8/57 reflects a stable in solid form; style is Unknown but Murphy's judgement on a debut juvenile with unknown profile is the single biggest x-factor in this race.

races.paceDynamic: Hackpen Hill is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner novice field and, with no serious rival disputing the lead, Kieran Shoemark should be able to dictate a comfortable, measured gallop from the front on Good to Firm ground at Salisbury. The pace is unlikely to be punishing — a single leader setting its own rhythm on fast ground typically produces a race where the front-runner can conserve energy through the middle section and quicken in the final two furlongs, making life very hard for hold-up horses needing a true end-to-end gallop to close. The field does contain more hold-up types than can realistically find their natural rearward position — Easy Answer and First Mate are genuine hold-up horses that have been redistributed to midfield on the map, meaning they will race closer than ideal and are unlikely to deliver a sustained late surge from off the pace. This race shape strongly favours horses who can race prominently or press the pace without expending too much early energy, and any debutant (Flick Of An Eye, Saturn Star, Forbidden Fire) with natural speed who slots in behind Hackpen Hill will have an ideal sightline on a track where getting a clear run matters.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hackpen Hill Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Hackpen Hill is allowed to stride clear from the gates and sets a controlled, solo tempo with no rivals pressuring him through the first two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Shoemark dictates a sustainable pace and the race becomes a stamina-sapping sprint from the two-furlong pole, suiting horses who have tracked efficiently and can quicken off a slow-medium pace; prominent racers with early foot inherit a favourable position and face minimal traffic problems.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Debutant Bursts Through
scenarios.trigger: If one of the three unraced types (Flick Of An Eye, Saturn Star, Forbidden Fire) shows natural early pace and takes up a prominent position to challenge or pass Hackpen Hill.
scenarios.body: A lightly-raced juvenile with raw speed can exploit an uncontested tempo by sitting just off the pace and unleashing a clean burst in the final furlong on good-to-firm ground; the Oisin Murphy partnership on Forbidden Fire (Balding, T14: 8/57) gives this scenario genuine danger money on debut.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If Easy Answer or First Mate, despite being displaced from their natural rear position, manage to find a clear passage and produce a sustained late run on ground that suits.
scenarios.body: Both horses have shown some form at this trip on similar going and if the pace does quicken enough to string the field out, a clean gap could materialise; however, both are racing out of their natural hold-up role mapped to midfield, which materially reduces the probability of a clean late finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Type Hits Gaps
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses entirely and the race fragments, allowing a midfield tracker to weave through a disorganised finish.
scenarios.body: Gold Reef City or Goodwood Meteor, both experienced campaigners at 6f on similar ground, could benefit from positional chaos if multiple leaders trade blows and leave the race open late; the scenario requires an untypical pace collapse which is unlikely given Hackpen Hill's confirmed front-running profile.

watchPoints.text: Forbidden Fire: Oisin Murphy on an Andrew Balding debutant at a yard firing (T14: 8/57) — if this juvenile shows early natural pace it will sit perfectly off Hackpen Hill's shoulder and could be a significant threat.

Easy Answer and First Mate: both are true hold-up horses mapped into midfield against their natural style; watch whether either drifts back to their genuine rear position at the start, which would effectively remove them from serious contention in a slowly-run race.

Hackpen Hill's hood: the application of headgear on a twice-raced front-runner is a flag — watch the pre-race demeanour and whether Shoemark gets a clean break, as a tardy start would fundamentally alter the entire race shape.

Gold Reef City vs Saturn Star (dual Beckett runners): Robbie Downey versus Hector Crouch within the same yard — the senior jockey's mount (Gold Reef City) typically signals the trainer's stronger hope and is worth tracking as the hold-up angle with the most realistic form claims.

Good to Firm surface confirmation: despite the race card listing Good, the going report consistently reads Good to Firm for the 2:30 6f — fast-ground suitability is confirmed for Hackpen Hill and Arctic Tsar (both sim-going 2/2 OK) but is an open question for Goodwood Meteor whose last run came on Soft.

races.name: Frazier Jones Wine Merchants Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: So Darn Hot
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who needs a genuine pace to close into; Ed Walker's 9/43 14-day strike rate is strong but this horse's recent form reads 0-6-7-0-5, and sim-going figures show limited impact, suggesting confidence should be tempered despite no going concern at 6f.

runners_data.name: Dr Strangelove
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with four of five recent runs producing a place at 6f to 7f; Tom Marquand is a key booking and his 4/17 trainer strike rate for Oliver Cole is solid, though stepping back to this 6f trip after two 7f runs is worth monitoring for whether he gets the trip sharply enough.

runners_data.name: Dandana
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner and pace-setter who won over this course-and-distance profile in her best form; tongue tie noted, Simon & Ed Crisford in good 14-day form, and 16 days since last run presents no freshness concern — she holds all the tactical cards here.

runners_data.name: Regional Rock
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced 3yo who has placed in all four career starts, including three at 6f on Good or Soft; Ralph Beckett's runner with Hector Crouch aboard shapes as the most dangerous chaser on pure form, and his sim-going record of 1W/3P in four comparable outings underlines his consistency in this ground.

runners_data.name: Golden Brown
runners_data.note: Prominent-style 3yo who won at 6f on Good ground and has placed twice at the trip; 60 days since last run is the primary concern, as a rusty reappearance could cost him the early foot he needs to hold his position against fresher rivals in a competitive field.

runners_data.name: An Outlaw's Grace
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who has shown ability at 6f on Good ground with three placed efforts in sim-going, but zero wins in 10 comparable outings tells its own story; with headgear noted (p) and a moderate pace likely, Sean Levey will need fortune to find a clear passage late enough to matter.

runners_data.name: Supreme King
runners_data.note: Veteran 6yo with strong recent placed form including three seconds in his last five runs, but pushed back from his natural prominent position here due to the field's concentration of front-rank types; his STYLE_FIT score of 0.93 flags a meaningful role compromise, and Oisin Murphy's ability to adapt in running offers the best chance of damage limitation from a difficult position.

races.paceDynamic: Dandana is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to challenge for the lead, shapes to control this race from the front at a pace of her own choosing on Good to Firm ground at Salisbury. Behind her, Dr Strangelove, Regional Rock, and Golden Brown are all natural prominent types who will jostle for position in the chasing group, creating a contest for slots two through four rather than a battle for the lead itself. Supreme King is a genuine prominent racer who, given the density of prominent types in this field, is unlikely to secure his natural position and will be shuffled further back than ideal, compromising his chance. With Dandana dictating an uncontested, measured gallop, this race shape strongly favours horses who can race prominently just off the pace and pounce in the final furlong — a true waiting or hold-up run from deep is made significantly harder when the pace is controlled and not pressured into becoming a true test.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dandana Leads, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Dandana sets a controlled, unchallenged pace and the prominent chasers fail to close the gap in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Dandana dictates every yard on her own terms, the moderate gallop suiting a horse capable of quickening off it, and the tight Salisbury straight giving chasers little time to close; horses tracking her closely at a length or two are best placed to capitalise if she weakens.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Chaser Swamps Them
scenarios.trigger: If the pace group bunches and one of the tracking prominent types produces a sharper turn of foot in the final 2f.
scenarios.body: Dr Strangelove or Regional Rock, racing just off Dandana's shoulder, benefits from cover and a genuine kick; their consistent placed form at 6f on Good ground makes them the most dangerous if Dandana's lead proves too slim to defend.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Fires Late
scenarios.trigger: If Dandana goes hard enough to string the field out and leave hold-up types with daylight to close.
scenarios.body: So Darn Hot or An Outlaw's Grace would need an unusually strong pace for Salisbury's 6f to generate the late fractions that suit their closing style; it is possible but against the dominant shape in this race.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Supreme King Defies Mapping
scenarios.trigger: If the race develops chaotically and Supreme King manages to secure a prominent pitch closer than anticipated.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires other prominent runners to check or miss the break, gifting Supreme King his natural position; his STYLE_FIT penalty and redistribution make this the least likely shape, though his recent placed form at 6f on Good ground means the form is not absent.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether any of Dr Strangelove, Regional Rock or Golden Brown applies pressure to Dandana in the opening furlong — if two or more push her early, the pace becomes genuinely searching and late closers So Darn Hot and An Outlaw's Grace come sharply into play.

Golden Brown's 60-day absence is the key fitness flag in this race; if he is ring-rusty he could drift out of his prominent position quickly and leave Ed Walker's yard with only So Darn Hot as a live runner.

Supreme King's redistribution to midfield is worth tracking from the stalls — if he breaks sharply and Oisin Murphy pushes him forward aggressively, he could reclaim his natural prominent pitch and become a far more potent threat than his mapped position suggests.

The going report consistently lists this race's conditions as Good to Firm rather than the stated Good — horses with a preference for faster ground (Dandana, Regional Rock) may have a subtle surface edge over those whose form reads best on easier going (Dr Strangelove, An Outlaw's Grace).

races.name: British Stallion Studs EBF Stonehenge Stakes (Listed Race)

runners_data.name: Dandyman Dan
runners_data.note: A natural front-runner with Good-ground form (3/5 on similar going) who has beaten just four rivals in his last two, so his likelihood of leading long at OR=96 in this company against classier pace rivals is limited; Kieran Shoemark will need to find a slot early and the 1m trip is a step up.

runners_data.name: Firehorse
runners_data.note: Won on Standard going and has only two runs to his name, so there is genuine uncertainty about stamina for the mile; Tom Marquand takes over and will likely try to dictate, but with Rocket Boy and Quest For Stars around him, getting a clear lead is far from guaranteed.

runners_data.name: My A'Ali Baba
runners_data.note: David Evans runner who holds a hold-up berth and arrives on 13 days' rest after an 11th-place effort at Goodwood; the two placings on soft ground hint at a stamina profile that could be activated if the pace truly combusts, but the 0W record on Good going is a mild concern.

runners_data.name: Quest For Stars
runners_data.note: Charlie Appleby's unbeaten juvenile (2W from 2 runs, both on Good) is the standout on form and Going record, and Connor Planas can afford to sit second or third and let the dust settle — a 10/27 T14 rate for Appleby keeps confidence measured but the raw form is hard to ignore.

runners_data.name: Rafe's Da Man
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's consistent type who won last time out over 7f on Good and has shown a knack for finishing into the places; Pat Dobbs is likely to secure a prominent pitch just off the pace battle rather than lead, which maps perfectly to the dominant scenario.

runners_data.name: Rocket Boy
runners_data.note: The classiest horse in the field on OR=120 with a winning debut on Good going; Marco Botti sends him here as the natural pace-setter and his superiority in ratings suggests he could dictate and sustain, but the mile trip and multi-leader dynamic both represent unknowns.

runners_data.name: Velociraptor
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's lightly-raced type won on Good and ran third, both over 7f, and David Probert will look to settle him prominently just off the leaders; the form is modest but the profile is tactically well-placed for a pace-collapse scenario.

runners_data.name: Scommessa Sicura
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy aboard Andrew Balding's improver who has been placed four times and finally won last time out; a 34-day absence is the one flag, but Murphy's ability to find cover and time a late run makes this horse one to respect if the front-runners exhaust each other.

races.paceDynamic: Rocket Boy (OR=120), Dandyman Dan, Firehorse, and Quest For Stars all carry strong front-running tendencies, meaning the pace from the gate at Salisbury's flat mile will be fierce and unrelenting from the outset. With four genuine leaders all wanting to occupy the same piece of real estate, there will be an early scramble for supremacy that almost certainly produces a true gallop rather than a tactical crawl — stamina will be examined long before the home straight. The one certainty is that whoever hits the front first will be pressured immediately, compressing the race into a sustained test of resolution rather than a sprint finish. This shape strongly favours hold-up and prominent runners who can conserve energy in the early stages and unleash a late run into a strung-out field — Scommessa Sicura, Rafe's Da Man, Velociraptor, and My A'Ali Baba all carry profiles that stand to benefit from the carnage up front.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace War Burns Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If the multi-runner pace battle produces a genuinely strong early tempo that softens the front-runners before the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Rocket Boy, Quest For Stars, and Dandyman Dan battle for supremacy across the first half-mile, draining each other's reserves, and the race is left for the prominent-to-hold-up brigade to pick up the pieces late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Leader Dictates Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Rocket Boy (OR=120) asserts early dominance and the other leaders fall in behind at a controlled, manageable tempo.
scenarios.body: Rocket Boy's class advantage and experience of winning on similar going allows him to set a metronomic pace and simply sustain it, with no rival able to reel him in from behind.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong but not catastrophic, allowing a horse travelling prominently just off the leaders to strike at the top of the straight.
scenarios.body: Rafe's Da Man or Velociraptor, having tracked without being embroiled in the early duel, gets a perfect tow into the straight and proves strongest of those in the chasing pack.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Springs Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly extreme and the race totally falls apart, leaving a closer to mow down beaten rivals in the final 100 yards.
scenarios.body: My A'Ali Baba, ridden quietly in rear by Callum Shepherd, gets a dream split through beaten horses late, but needs the pace to be truly brutal to make up the ground.

watchPoints.text: Rocket Boy and Quest For Stars are both natural leaders — watch at the break to see who asserts first, as whoever gets squeezed back early will have their winning chance significantly compromised.

Scommessa Sicura has the most complete profile for this race shape — if Oisin Murphy gets a clean passage to challenge entering the straight, the hold-up style becomes a potent weapon against the pace-depleted leaders.

The genuine going is Good To Firm (riders' reports consistent across the card) despite the race description showing Good — horses who have shown a preference for softer conditions, including My A'Ali Baba, may find the surface quicker than ideal.

Rafe's Da Man's prominent style is well-suited here, but Richard Hannon's T14 strike rate of 8/56 is modest — be alert to whether Pat Dobbs receives riding instructions that push him closer to the pace than expected.

The step up from 6-7f to 1m is untested for every runner in this field — any horse that has shaped like it would get a longer trip (staying on at finish) in its form history gains a meaningful edge over those that have been finishing off fast.

races.name: Molson Coors Pembroke Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Bold Shout
runners_data.note: Clive Cox's lightly raced three-year-old showed a 4-4 form line without winning, but both efforts came at 6-7f on similar or softer ground and the step to good to firm is untested; style unknown, so early positioning is the key variable under Hector Crouch — a forward break could prove decisive here.

runners_data.name: It's A Mugs Game
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up runner who last ran 12 days ago and brings experience of 6f on firm ground; Sean Levey has to navigate a crowded rearward group and will need daylight at the two-furlong pole to maximise this horse's late effort.

runners_data.name: Kodicall
runners_data.note: Placed on good to firm over 6f in his most recent outing and has sim-going form to draw on; another hold-up type who, like others in this field, will find natural rear-ground contested — Taylor Fisher will need to be patient and hope the pace is genuine enough to deliver a finishing run.

runners_data.name: Annie Sioux
runners_data.note: Debutant for Clive Cox with Tom Marquand aboard — going preference and running style entirely unknown, making her the principal wildcard; Cox has two runners in the race and Marquand's instructions on how to place her in the early exchanges will largely shape her chance.

runners_data.name: Gris De Chine
runners_data.note: The race's pivotal horse — a confirmed prominent-type whose front-running role is its clear strength; OR of 59 is significantly below the novice field's upper tier and a style-fit tag signals she is racing slightly out of her natural zone, but the absence of rivals willing to match her stride for stride from the gates makes her positional advantage real regardless of bare ratings.

runners_data.name: Just Dreaming
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's hold-up specialist arrives nine days after her last run having finished 5-7-5 in her most recent starts; she is redistributed to midfield on the pace map because the rear of the field is congested with true closers, and Oliver Carmichael's claim may not compensate for the compromised ground-finding position she is likely to face.

runners_data.name: Remi Mae
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's mare owns genuine form at 6f on good ground — three placed efforts in six sim-going starts — and Oisin Murphy represents a significant jockey upgrade; her hold-up profile is her natural style but, with the field stacked at the rear, she is mapped to midfield and will need a clear path through traffic to deploy her best form.

races.paceDynamic: Gris De Chine is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner novice and will aim to dictate from the gates over Salisbury's straight six on good to firm ground, setting a measured, uncontested tempo that gives her every chance to control the race from flag to finish. The hold-up contingent is notably crowded: Remi Mae, Just Dreaming, and Kodicall are all natural hold-up types, meaning most of the field will be tracking or chasing rather than forcing genuine competition for the lead. Annie Sioux and Bold Shout are unproven on style and could land anywhere in the early order, but neither is likely to press Gris De Chine hard. The resulting shape — a lone, uncontested pace-setter on fast ground over a sprint trip — strongly favours prominent racers and those with the class and acceleration to pick off a potentially well-set leader in the final furlong; pure closers face a stiff task given the field holds far more hold-up types than the race can accommodate, with Remi Mae and Just Dreaming the most likely to be denied their natural ground-covering role at the rear.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Gris De Chine controls unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Gris De Chine breaks cleanly and is allowed to bowl along at her own tempo with no rival willing to close the door early.
scenarios.body: She sets a fair but sustainable gallop and, with no genuine challenger on her outside, holds a decisive positional advantage entering the final two furlongs; horses with the class to quicken from a prominent pitch have the clearest route to her.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late class arrives on time
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is strong enough for one of the hold-up runners to generate momentum off the turn and finish powerfully through tired horses.
scenarios.body: A decent tempo combined with good-to-firm ground can produce a closing surge from a horse with raw ability, but the crowded hold-up group means only the classiest finisher gets a clean run and clear daylight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace collapse, race falls apart
scenarios.trigger: If Gris De Chine's early splits are too slow and the field concertinas, turning the race into a messy sprint for home.
scenarios.body: A compressed field on quick ground rewards sharp acceleration and a forward position; a horse with a prominent pitch and a change of gear becomes decisive when the race ignites only inside the final furlong.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses swamp the field
scenarios.trigger: If Gris De Chine fades sharply and a wall of closers arrives simultaneously to swamp the principals.
scenarios.body: This outcome requires the leader to set a genuinely taxing pace that drains her own reserves, allowing multiple hold-up runners to arrive together; given the true hold-up types are redistributed and may not achieve their natural pitch, a clean sweep from the rear is an unlikely outcome.

watchPoints.text: Gris De Chine's gate break — if she stumbles or misses the start she loses her entire race shape advantage and Bold Shout or Annie Sioux could inherit an unplanned lead.
Remi Mae's route through traffic is the critical late factor; Oisin Murphy will have to thread a needle in a compressed hold-up group to deliver the run her form merits.
Annie Sioux is a complete unknown on debut and Tom Marquand's decision on whether to deploy her prominently or conservatively could reshape the whole complexion of the race.

Good-to-firm ground at Salisbury on the day — connections confirmed the 4:00 6f surface — means early fractions will be quick and any horse that overcooks the opening two furlongs risks weakening sharply, particularly relevant for Gris De Chine setting the tempo alone.

Trainer Clive Cox runs two runners (Bold Shout, Annie Sioux) in the same race; watch for any market move on either as stable confidence signals and whether jockey bookings suggest which is the stable's primary hope.

races.name: British Stallion Studs EBF Upavon Fillies' Stakes (Listed Race)

runners_data.name: Alla Stella
runners_data.note: Prescott's hold-up filly brings solid placed form over 10-12f on soft and good ground but has yet to win in six starts; her best chance comes if the pace stretches the field and she can pick off tiring rivals through Salisbury's straight.

runners_data.name: Goldilocks Cen
runners_data.note: Archie Watson's 4yo has been pushed into a midfield mapping by redistribution — she is a natural hold-up horse with a poor recent record on good ground (0W0P in five relevant runs) and a modest OR of 86 makes her an unlikely winner here.

runners_data.name: Regal Charm
runners_data.note: Henry Candy's 4yo has won and placed over 10f on this going profile and is drawn to press Felicitas from a prominent position, giving her the tactical advantage of sitting on the pace with proven class at this level.

runners_data.name: Annastarzy
runners_data.note: Hannon's 3-year-old has won three of her last four on good ground but is a natural prominent racer who, given the crowded pace picture, is unlikely to secure her preferred position and the style-fit discount applies materially to her chances today.

runners_data.name: Felicitas
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's 3yo is the confirmed pace-setter with the OR advantage at 103; her recent course of 1-127 shows she can both lead and stay, and uncontested control of the early fractions on fast ground suits her profile markedly — the 59-day break is worth monitoring.

runners_data.name: Miss Scott
runners_data.note: Gosden-trained 3yo with a compact but strong form record of 1-21, winning over 10f on good ground; likely to sit prominently under Murphy and could prove the most dangerous challenger to any front-runner in the straight.

runners_data.name: On Message
runners_data.note: Beckett's 3yo won over 8f and has placed over 10f on good ground; she races hold-up and her best hope rests on the pace being strong enough to create a genuine late opportunity through the straight — her 1-1374 recent form shows inconsistency.

races.paceDynamic: Felicitas is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, she will be able to dictate terms at a measured, sustainable gallop on good to firm ground over 1m2f at Salisbury. Miss Scott and Regal Charm are the likeliest prominent-position horses to sit just behind her, meaning the race will be run in an orderly procession rather than a contested fashion. The field nominally contains more pace than the map can accommodate — Annastarzy and Goldilocks Cen are natural prominent and hold-up types respectively but have been redistributed toward midfield given the race shape, meaning neither is likely to operate in their ideal slot. This uncontested, measured tempo is the defining tactical reality: horses with the class to travel prominently or close enough to Felicitas without burning reserves — and the ability to sustain their effort through Salisbury's long straight — are the profile that benefits most, with true hold-up horses relying on a finish that may never truly materialise.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Felicitas Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Felicitas bowls along at a fair but unhurried pace with no horse willing to press her, setting up a test of sustained galloping class rather than a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: Felicitas controls every yard, the race unfolds at her tempo, and horses close enough to track her cruise into contention through the long straight; prominent racers with proven class over this trip are perfectly positioned.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Grinders Collide
scenarios.trigger: If Miss Scott and Regal Charm push forward aggressively early, creating slightly more pressure on Felicitas and turning the race into a more genuine test of stamina.
scenarios.body: A fractionally stronger pace than Scenario A means the race becomes a thorough 1m2f grind; horses with deep staying reserves and proven course-distance form over this sort of flat, testing straight come to the fore.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough that prominent and front-running horses tie each other up in the straight, leaving a window for hold-up horses to pick up late ground.
scenarios.body: On Message, operating off a true staying gallop, finds room to close from off the pace; Alla Stella's hold-up profile with Prescott's patient horsemanship could also see her finish well if the fractions are honest.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Annastarzy Breaks Free
scenarios.trigger: If Annastarzy, a natural prominent racer shuffled toward midfield by the redistribution, manages to reclaim a forward position early and the race evolves in a way that suits front-of-field runners through the straight.
scenarios.body: Racing out of her ideal role reduces Annastarzy's chance materially, but if she does secure a prominent pitch her recent winning form on good ground gives her a live chance; Goldilocks Cen faces similar out-of-role issues from the back and is unlikely to feature.

watchPoints.text: Felicitas's 59-day layoff combined with an uncontested lead could mean she either over-relaxes and flattens out, or bounces fresh — Shoemark's handling of the pace in the opening half-mile will be the defining moment of the race.

Miss Scott was beaten only a length at Group 3 level on her last start and Murphy's positive riding style could put her in a dangerous position stalking Felicitas — watch whether she is placed to challenge before the final furlong.

Regal Charm has an OR of 99 and has won over this trip on soft and good — if Candy targets a prominent position early, she and Miss Scott between them could create more pressure on Felicitas than the pace map anticipates, pushing toward Scenario B.

Annastarzy's redistribution from prominent to midfield is a critical watch point at the start — if she breaks sharply and Joe Leavy elects to push forward regardless, she could disrupt the expected orderly shape behind Felicitas.

Alla Stella's trainer record of 4/23 over 14 days and an 11-day turnaround suggests Prescott has this filly ready; if the pace is quicker than expected her closing profile could see her finish faster than her mid-race position suggests.

races.name: Champagne Joseph Perrier Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Londoner
runners_data.note: OR 86 front-runner who must fight for the lead against Eupator; his 15-run record on similar going shows zero wins and just one place, a significant flag, though headgear (hood/p) suggests he needs to be covered up or switched on — here he has no choice but to bowl along.

runners_data.name: Fox Avatar
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy booked for this Roger Varian runner who won this exact trip at Sandown and ran well fresh before (LR 44d); prominent by nature and that style may expose him if the lead pair set a punishing clip, but his class and the top jockey make him the main danger from close-up.

runners_data.name: Miss Tonnerre
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare from Ed Walker who has been off 77 days; her best form has come on good ground, she steps back up to 1m2f which suits, and a strong finishing run from the rear is her only gear — she needs the pace to truly collapse in front.

runners_data.name: Almekarem
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's hold-up gelding has won on good ground at 10f and is lightly raced over this slightly longer trip; ran just 11 days ago at Goodwood which shows he is fit and ready, and Luke Morris will likely drop him in last before producing him late.

runners_data.name: Eupator
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's front-runner has contested pace on good and firm ground before and his 15-run similar-going record shows two places but no wins, raising doubts about whether fighting for the lead here serves him well; Sean Levey will need to judge whether to force the issue with Londoner or concede and slot in.

runners_data.name: Carnival Day
runners_data.note: Jim Boyle's prominent racer has solid form at the trip — placed over 10f on good and soft — and Pat Cosgrave will look to track the leading pair from a handy position; his one-win-four-place record on similar going suggests he finds a way to be competitive but rarely seals the deal.

runners_data.name: Mythical Bird
runners_data.note: Hughie Morrison's prominent type has two placed efforts from six at 10f on good ground and is stepping up to 1m2f for the first time in this company; the trainer's 0/4 over 14 days is a minor caution, but the horse's consistent placed form on similar going keeps him relevant if the pace is testing enough.

races.paceDynamic: Londoner and Eupator are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the early lead from the gates, creating a genuinely competitive gallop rather than a soft, uncontested tempo — on Good to Firm ground at Salisbury over 1m2f, that honest pace is likely to be sustained rather than compressed into a late sprint. Fox Avatar and Carnival Day will push up prominently just behind the duelling leaders, meaning the first two furlongs will be actively contested and the field will string out early. The mid-to-rear section — Miss Tonnerre, Almekarem, and Mythical Bird — will likely be held up at a comfortable distance, waiting for the pace to tell on those at the front. This race shape clearly favours hold-up and come-from-behind profiles: if the two front-runners burn each other off through the downhill section and into the straight, there will be a premium on horses who conserve energy and finish strongly, making Almekarem, Miss Tonnerre, and Mythical Bird the styles to focus on.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Londoner and Eupator push each other along at a genuine clip and both capitulate inside the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: The contested lead burns through both front-runners early on the fast ground, leaving them empty as the home straight arrives; hold-up horses who were settled in rear have the energy reserves to sweep through.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is honest but not damaging, and one prominent racer conserves enough to outstay the closers.
scenarios.body: Fox Avatar or Carnival Day, tracking just off the lead, avoids the worst of the early attrition and has enough class or stamina to hold on as closers make their run; Fox Avatar's win form at this trip gives him the edge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Lone Front-Runner Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Eupator or Londoner quickly establishes clear supremacy and the other capitulates early, allowing the remaining leader to dictate at their own tempo.
scenarios.body: A solo leader sets a controlled, even gallop that never truly tests stamina, and the race becomes a test of cruising speed rather than finishing kick; Londoner's OR 86 gives him the class edge if he gets an uncontested lead.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Grind, Stamina Test
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is relentless throughout and the race becomes a true stamina slog that eliminates sprinting types.
scenarios.body: A gruelling tempo on the fast ground sees the entire field spread out and those with the most genuine stamina at 1m2f prevail; Mythical Bird and Almekarem, both with solid form at the trip, are the main beneficiaries.

watchPoints.text: Londoner and Eupator — watch the first two furlongs closely; if neither concedes the lead and they race in earnest, the race will be won from the back of the field.

Fox Avatar is 44 days since his last run and comes from a stable that has been winning at a solid clip; if he travels sweetly behind the speed on his reappearance, Oisin Murphy could deliver him at the perfect moment.
Almekarem ran just 11 days ago at Goodwood — monitor his paddock appearance for any signs of residual tiredness, as a quick turnaround at this level can leave a horse short.

Salisbury's home straight is notably testing despite the flat classification; horses who are beaten early in the straight rarely rally, making the position rounding the final bend a critical moment to observe.

Going reports confirm Good to Firm all day at Salisbury — faster than the declared Good, which increases the premium on horses with proven fast-ground form and may accelerate the fade of any front-runner who over-races.
